- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or shift downward by 1–3%.
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., >90.00) with sentiment mostly positive (≥0.67), it often overshoots; cap forecast at 92–95% of prior peak or adjust downward 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows sharp drop after spike (e.g., 90→75), model often fails to correct; add lagged mean reversion term: forecast = prior + 0.7×(true - prior) if true drops >5%.
- When sentiment turns negative (e.g., 0.00) and model is rising, forecast often misreads sentiment; reduce forecast by 1–3% per negative sentiment day.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows strong volatility (e.g., 85→95→80), apply “sentiment-triggered volatility buffer”: add ±2–5% jitter if sentiment swings >0.5.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history: if last 3–5 days are trending up, don’t assume continuation; use sentiment to trigger mean reversion if sentiment drops below 0.33.
